text: Preface

title: Bioconductor Community Handbook
text:
Welcome
Welcome to the Bioconductor Community Handbook.
This handbook is a collaborative effort to capture and share knowledge about the Bioconductor community, its practices, and its resources. It is intended for anyone interested in contributing to or learning from the Bioconductor community, whether you are a seasoned contributor or a newcomer.
This book was initiated during a BioFAIR Collaboration Fest held at The Open University on 15-17 September 2026. It began as an effort to capture FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) practices not covered by existing Bioconductor materials, but discussions broadened its scope into a handbook bringing together key aspects of community practice in one place.
The structure of this handbook is inspired from The Turing Way, referring to it for more general guidance on open source software development, data science, and reproducible research. It is intended to unify this combined knowledge under one common roof while signposting to more specialised guidance maintained by Bioconductor and other communities.

title: Guide for Communication
text:
This guide will provide practical advice for communicating within the Bioconductor community and with other communities.
It will define shared language, identify where to ask questions and share needs, and describe how users, developers, trainers, and maintainers can collaborate effectively within and beyond Bioconductor.

title: Communicating with the community
text: This section will introduce communication practices, resources, and pathways for coordinating work and building effective relationships with other community members.

title: Communicating with other communities
text: This section will introduce communication practices, resources, and pathways for coordinating work and building effective relationships with other projects and communities.

title: Guide for FAIR Practices
text: As part of the Bioconductor community, we develop and maintain open-source software, data, and training resources. By applying the FAIR principles – Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable – this guide will cover practices and resources supporting users and developers in making those resources easier to discover, access, integrate, and reuse within and beyond the Bioconductor ecosystem. The following sections describe processes, resources, and checklists for producing FAIR Bioconductor tools, wrappers and workflows, including integrations with other software ecosystems.

title: 1  Interoperable file types
text: Preferred file types for disk-based storage of R objects and interoperability with other programming languages and software ecosystems will be documented here.

title: 2  Bioconductor in Galaxy
section: 2.3 Galaxy file types for Bioconductor objects
text:
2.3 Galaxy file types for Bioconductor objects
How are R objects stored on disk in Galaxy? What are the preferred file types for interoperability with other programming languages and software ecosystems?
For example, this GitHub issue has been discussing insecure aspects of RData files. While those are the default file type for R objects, they are not interoperable with other programming languages and software ecosystems. Instead, the loom file format has gained popularity as a preferred file type for disk-based storage of R objects, and is interoperable with other programming languages and software ecosystems
